compiled_state.title: As an operator, each sub-branch passes its own scoped review with autonomous resolution before merging into the session branch; escalations are handled atomically and continue to the next sub-branch
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Wire per-sub-branch scoped review with discriminated outcomes. Invoke `validate-review-output.sh` schema validation, run the autonomous resolution loop, return `MERGED`/`ESCALATED`/`ERROR`, and annotate the aggregate PR on escalation.

**Why**: Per-sub-branch scoped review is the core fidelity improvement of this epic. The discriminated outcomes pattern lets the Phase F/G loop continue past one failing sub-branch without halting the whole tier.

**Scope**:
- IN: Per-sub-branch review invokes `validate-review-output.sh` JSON-schema validation against `reviewer-findings.json` before recording `REVIEW_RESULT`; autonomous resolution loop honors `review.max_resolution_attempts` (default 5) with floor-guard (use minimum 1 attempt + log warning when configured 0); discriminated return value (`MERGED`/`ESCALATED`/`ERROR`) consumed at Phase F/G loop level; **escalation atomicity ordering**: (1) write `SUBBRANCH_ESCALATED: <sub-branch> reason=<...>` ticket comment FIRST, (2) update aggregate draft PR `BLOCKED_SUBBRANCHES:` annotation SECOND, (3) continue to next sub-branch THIRD; **ticket comment is the authoritative single source of truth** — S7's `COMPACTION_RESUME` reconciles PR annotation from ticket comments on resume; `ESCALATED` does NOT halt the tier loop.
- OUT: Schema validation infrastructure itself (depends on 677d via SC13); hermetic-repro ordering (S11); leak detection (S9).

## Done Definitions

- When complete, each sub-branch's review invokes `validate-review-output.sh` schema validation against `reviewer-findings.json` before `REVIEW_RESULT` is recorded; schema failures trigger 677d's re-dispatch loop
  ← Satisfies: "Per-sub-branch review invokes validate-review-output.sh JSON-schema validation"
- When complete, the autonomous resolution loop runs with `review.max_resolution_attempts` (default 5) and applies a floor-guard of 1 attempt with a warning log when the config is 0
  ← Satisfies: "Autonomous resolution loop with review.max_resolution_attempts (default 5; floor-guard 1 when configured 0)"
- When complete, per-sub-branch review returns a discriminated `MERGED`/`ESCALATED`/`ERROR` value consumed at the Phase F/G loop level; on `ESCALATED`, the orchestrator writes `SUBBRANCH_ESCALATED:` ticket comment FIRST, updates aggregate-PR `BLOCKED_SUBBRANCHES:` annotation SECOND, then continues to the next sub-branch — ticket comment is the authoritative source of truth
  ← Satisfies: "Discriminated MERGED/ESCALATED/ERROR outcome consumed at Phase F/G loop level"
- When complete, regression test asserts /sprint per-story review behavior is unchanged when `review.max_resolution_attempts` is modified for debug-everything tuning (config is per-sub-branch / per-story, not per-session)
  ← Satisfies: "Each sub-branch passes its own scoped review"
- Unit tests written and passing for floor-guard, discriminated outcomes, and escalation ordering
  ← Satisfies: "Per-sub-branch review with discriminated outcomes"

## Considerations

- [Testing] Discriminated return-value routing at Phase F/G loop level needs unit-test coverage covering MERGED, ESCALATED, ERROR continuation paths
- [Reliability] Escalation atomicity: crash between step (1) and step (2) is recoverable — COMPACTION_RESUME reads ticket comment and reconciles PR annotation; document this contract in the resolution loop
- [Maintainability] `review.max_resolution_attempts` is a shared config key with /sprint; document that the value applies per-sub-branch/per-story (not per-session) and add a regression test asserting sprint behavior is not affected

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
